name: Uzziah
charge: Going into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense, which appertaineth not unto the king but to the priests the sons of Aaron; and raging at the priests who withstood him
summary: Uzziah was made king at sixteen and reigned fifty-two years; as long as he sought God in the days of Zechariah, God made him prosper, against the Philistines, Arabians and Mehunims, in towers, wells, husbandry and a great army with engines of war (2 Chronicles 26:1-15). When he was strong his heart was lifted up, and he went into the temple to burn incense, which belonged only to the priests (2 Chronicles 26:16). When Azariah and eighty priests withstood him he raged with the censer in his hand, and leprosy broke out on his forehead; he lived as a leper, cut off from the house of the Lord, until he died (2 Chronicles 26:17-21).
offenseFull: All the people of Judah made Uzziah king at sixteen in place of Amaziah, and he did right and sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God; as long as he sought the Lord, God made him prosper (2 Chronicles 26:1-5). This Zechariah was a different man from the priest Joash killed. Uzziah is like Joash, who did well while he had the guidance of Jehoiada. All the wise kings consulted with spiritual men; David consulted with every leader (1 Chronicles 13:1), and by wise counsel you make your war (Proverbs 24:5-6). Prosperity comes from the Most High, and it lasts only as long as a man keeps seeking Him.

He broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod and built cities among the Philistines, God helped him against the Philistines, the Arabians and the Mehunims, the Ammonites paid gifts, and his name spread to the entrance of Egypt (2 Chronicles 26:6-8). Jehoram had lost Edom and Elath; Uzziah restored Elath to Judah (2 Chronicles 26:2). He built towers, dug wells for his cattle and loved husbandry, a picture of the blessings of Deuteronomy 28 as the Lord made the land fruitful. His army numbered three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, with shields, spears, helmets and slings, and engines invented by cunning men to shoot arrows and great stones; his fame spread far, for the Lord helped him wonderfully until he became strong (2 Chronicles 26:9-15). Together with Jeroboam II in the north, the two kingdoms held borders close to those of David and Solomon; the Lord was giving His people another chance before He began to unleash judgments.

But when he was strong his heart was lifted up to his destruction, and he went into the temple to burn incense on the altar of incense (2 Chronicles 26:16). He got big-headed, a Judahite acting like a Levite. The king was to write a copy of the law and read it all the days of his life, so that his heart would not be lifted up above his brothers (Deuteronomy 17:18-20); the greater you are, the more you should humble yourself (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). Only the seed of Aaron could offer incense, lest a man end like Korah (Numbers 16:40), and the stranger who came near the priest’s office was to die (Numbers 18:7). Azariah the priest and eighty valiant priests withstood him and told him it did not belong to him, to leave the sanctuary, for he had trespassed and it would not be for his honour. Then Uzziah was angry, with a censer in his hand (2 Chronicles 26:17-19). He had beaten nations and would not be corrected by men he counted lower than himself, and he was ready to set fire to the priests of God.
judgmentFull: While he was angry with the priests, the leprosy rose up in his forehead before them beside the incense altar. The priests saw it and thrust him out, and he hurried out himself, because the Lord had struck him (2 Chronicles 26:19-20). He that is soon angry deals foolishly (Proverbs 14:17); one act out of a quick temper cost him a lifetime. The fear of the Lord goes before the obtaining of authority, but roughness and pride is the losing of it, and the Lord brings strange calamities on the proud (Ecclesiasticus 10:13, 21).

He was a leper to the day of his death and lived in a separate house, cut off from the house of the Lord, and Jotham his son was over the king’s house, judging the people (2 Chronicles 26:21). The law said the leper must dwell alone outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46); he was still king in name but could no longer sit on the throne, and leprosy is not merely white skin but a slow deterioration of the whole body. The Lord puts down the mighty from their seats (Luke 1:52). Isaiah wrote the rest of his acts, and they buried him in the field of burial belonging to the kings, not in their sepulchres, because they said he was a leper (2 Chronicles 26:22-23). Stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. In the year king Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up (Isaiah 6:1).

text.text: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah.
He built Eloth, and restored it to Judah, after that the king slept with his fathers.
Sixteen years old was Uzziah when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Amaziah did.
And he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the Lord, God made him to prosper.
And he went forth and warred against the Philistines, and brake down the wall of Gath, and the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod, and built cities about Ashdod, and among the Philistines.
And God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians that dwelt in Gur–baal, and the Mehunims.
And the Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziah: and his name spread abroad even to the entering in of Egypt; for he strengthened himself exceedingly.
Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, and at the valley gate, and at the turning of the wall, and fortified them.

Also he built towers in the desert, and digged many wells: for he had much cattle, both in the low country, and in the plains: husbandmen also, and vine dressers in the mountains, and in Carmel: for he loved husbandry.

Moreover Uzziah had an host of fighting men, that went out to war by bands, according to the number of their account by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the ruler, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king’s captains.
The whole number of the chief of the fathers of the mighty men of valour were two thousand and six hundred.
And under their hand was an army, three hundred thousand and seven thousand and five hundred, that made war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
And Uzziah prepared for them throughout all the host shields, and spears, and helmets, and habergeons, and bows, and slings to cast stones.

And he made in Jerusalem engines, invented by cunning men, to be on the towers and upon the bulwarks, to shoot arrows and great stones withal. And his name spread far abroad; for he was marvellously helped, till he was strong.
But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the Lord his God, and went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense.
And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the Lord, that were valiant men:

And they withstood Uzziah the king, and said unto him, It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither shall it be for thine honour from the Lord God.
